local function parse_file(path, scope, category, plugin_override)
  local content = read(path)
  if not content then
    return {}
  end

  local plugin = plugin_override or vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":t:r")
  local meta = META_FILES[plugin] == true
  local records = {}
  local heading, columns, awaiting_separator = nil, nil, false
  -- In a repo sheet the category travels with the section. Before the first
  -- matching `##` heading there is none, and lines before it (title table,
  -- table of contents) belong to none either.
  local section_category = category
  -- Scoped to the section, not to the file: a sheet can hold one unverifiable
  -- table next to five ordinary ones, and `Keymaps/VisualMulti.md` does.
  local not_live = false

  local lines = vim.split(content:gsub("\r", ""), "\n", { plain = true })

  -- plugin. Reading both would double-count every binding — in
  -- `:Bindings status`, in the drift report, as two identical picker rows. The
  -- repo sheet wins: it is the source, the cheatsheet is the copy.

functions.snippet:
function M.wildcard_pattern(token, kind)
  if not token:find("%*") and not token:find("<.->") then
    return nil
  end
  local literal = token:gsub("<.->", ""):gsub("%*", "")
  if #literal:gsub("[^%w_]", "") < 3 then
    return nil
  end
  local class = WILDCARD_CLASS[kind] or WILDCARD_CLASS.command
  local escaped = token:gsub("[%^%$%(%)%%%.%[%]%+%-%?]", "%%%0")
  -- The escape above turned `<name>` into `<name>` still (angle brackets are
  -- not pattern syntax), so both placeholder forms are replaced here.
  escaped = escaped:gsub("<.->", class):gsub("%*", class)
  return "^" .. escaped .. "$"
end

nodes.name: repo.lua
nodes.summary: The fourth drift axis' one primitive: "is this literal written anywhere in that source tree?" — a plain string search over a checkout's `.lua`/`.vim` files,…
nodes.body:
**Why this exists at all.** `drift.lua`'s live axis can only judge a
documented binding whose owning plugin is already loaded in THIS session
(its module doc, point 4). Everything else is reported as "skipped", which
is honest but empty: in a normal session that is the large majority of the
personal plugins, so most of the corpus is never actually checked by
anything. Reading the plugin's own checkout answers those, because a
checkout is on disk whether or not lazy.nvim ever got around to loading it.

**Deliberately weaker than the live axis, and not a replacement for it.**
`nvim_get_keymap` answers "is this registered"; a grep answers "does this
string appear in the source". The second is a proxy for the first and gets
it wrong in both directions:
  - false negative: an lhs assembled at runtime (`prefix .. "v"`, a key
    read from a user config table) is genuinely registered and simply not
    greppable. This is the known cost, and `drift.lua` labels the section
    with it rather than pretending the axis is authoritative.
  - false positive (i.e. a real drift silently accepted): the literal
    appears in a comment, a test fixture, or the plugin's own README-in-
    Lua. Accepted on purpose — the whole module's stance is that a missed
    finding is cheaper than a wrong one.

**Only quoted occurrences count.** Both things this looks for — a keymap
lhs and a user command name — are always written as string literals at
their registration site (`vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>iv", …)`,
`composer.verb("Images", …)`, `["<leader>iv"] = …`). Searching for the
bare word instead was measurably useless for commands: `:Images`
case-folded matches "images" in every second line of images.nvim, so
every command would count as found and the axis would report nothing ever.

**Only `.lua`/`.vim`.** A plugin's own `doc/`, `README.md` and cheatsheets
describe the same bindings this corpus documents; matching them would mean
confirming documentation against documentation. Restricting to source
extensions excludes them without needing a path-based exception list.

functions.name: index
functions.snippet:
local function index(dir)
  local cached = cache[dir]
  if cached then
    return cached
  end

  local ok, files = pcall(collect_recursive.files, dir, { ignore = prune })
  local chunks, count = {}, 0
  if ok then
    for _, path in ipairs(files) do
      local stat = vim.uv.fs_stat(path)
      if stat and (stat.size or 0) <= MAX_FILE_BYTES then
        local content = read(path)
        if content then
          count = count + 1
          chunks[#chunks + 1] = content
        end
      end
    end
  end

  -- Joined with a newline so a match can never straddle two files' bytes.
  local tree = { text = table.concat(chunks, "\n"), files = count }
  cache[dir] = tree
  return tree
end

nodes.name: report.lua
nodes.summary: `:Bindings report` — the same drift run `:Bindings check` shows in a viewer, written to a Markdown file instead.
nodes.body:
Why it exists: the 2026-09-02 drift report was assembled by hand out of a
headless run (`nvim --headless -c "lua ... drift.check"`, output
redirected, run header and counts typed in front of it). That hand work is
what this module does — run header, counts by finding kind, and
`drift.describe`'s unchanged text as an appendix.

What it deliberately does NOT do is judge the findings. Which of them is a
real documentation gap and which is a tool defect or an expected effect
(a buffer-local UI that is not open, a lazy trigger that never fired) is a
reading, and that reading is the part a handwritten report is worth
writing for. This file produces the measured half so the person only has
to add the other one.

The appendix is a ```text block rather than Markdown tables on purpose:
`drift.describe` aligns its columns with `%-22s`, and that alignment is
the only structure the raw report has. Re-cast as tables it would be
longer and read worse.

User-facing output is German, deliberately and consistently across every
string of `:Bindings` (see the note in init.lua).

functions.snippet:
function M.resolve_path(out)
  local dir_or_file = (out and out ~= "") and out or config.report_dir()
  -- `expand_path` rather than `vim.fn.expand()`: `out` is a command argument,
  -- and only `~`/`$VAR` are meant to expand in it. `vim.fn.expand()` would
  -- also resolve `%` to the current buffer's name, quietly writing the report
  -- somewhere the caller never named.
  local expanded = require("lib.nvim.cross.fs.expand_path")(dir_or_file)
  local abs = vim.fs.normalize(vim.fn.fnamemodify(expanded, ":p"))

  if vim.fn.isdirectory(abs) == 1 then
    abs =
      vim.fs.joinpath((abs:gsub("/$", "")), ("BINDINGS-DRIFT-%s.md"):format(os.date("%Y-%m-%d")))
  elseif not abs:match("%.%w+$") then
    abs = abs .. ".md"
  end

  return abs
end

local function pending_phases()
  local ok, startup = pcall(require, "startup")
  if not ok or type(startup) ~= "table" or type(startup.pending) ~= "function" then
    return {}
  end
  local ok_call, marks = pcall(startup.pending)
  if not ok_call or type(marks) ~= "table" then

  for _, m in ipairs(marks) do

  end
  table.sort(labels)
  return labels
end

params.name: opts
params.type: { plugin?: string, repo?: boolean, repo_root?: string, scope?: "personal"|"extern"|"all", out?: string }|nil

functions.snippet:
function M.write(opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  local path = M.resolve_path(opts.out)

  local dir = vim.fs.dirname(path)
  if vim.fn.isdirectory(dir) ~= 1 and vim.fn.mkdir(dir, "p") ~= 1 then
    return nil, ("Verzeichnis nicht anlegbar: %s"):format(dir), nil
  end

  local t0 = vim.uv.hrtime()
  local findings, skipped, source_reason, repo_info, scope_info =
    drift.check(opts.plugin, { repo = opts.repo, repo_root = opts.repo_root, scope = opts.scope })
  local ms = (vim.uv.hrtime() - t0) / 1e6

  local lines = M.render(findings, skipped, source_reason, repo_info, {
    plugin = opts.plugin,
    duration_ms = ms,
    scope_info = scope_info,
  })

  -- `writefile` returns 0 on success and -1 on failure, and throws for an
  -- unwritable path -- both have to be caught, or a failed report reads as a
  -- written one.
  local ok, res = pcall(vim.fn.writefile, lines, path)
  if not ok then
    return nil, tostring(res), nil
  end
  if res ~= 0 then
    return nil, ("konnte nicht schreiben: %s"):format(path), nil
  end

  return path, nil, #findings
end

local function matches(value, pattern)
  return value:lower():find(pattern:lower(), 1, true) ~= nil
end

functions.name: scan_file
functions.snippet:
local function scan_file(root, path, pattern, hits)
  local content = read(path)
  if not content then
    return
  end
  local lineno = 0
  for line in (content:gsub("\r", "") .. "\n"):gmatch("([^\n]*)\n") do
    lineno = lineno + 1
    if matches(line, pattern) then
      hits[#hits + 1] = { root = root, path = path, line = lineno, text = vim.trim(line) }
    end
  end
end
functions.summary: Hold one file against `pattern`, line by line.

functions.name: M.search
functions.snippet:
function M.search(pattern, roots)
  local hits = {}
  if not pattern or pattern == "" then
    return hits
  end

  for _, root in ipairs(roots or config.roots()) do
    if vim.fn.isdirectory(root) == 1 then
      for _, f in ipairs(collect_recursive.files(root)) do
        if f:match("%.md$") then
          scan_file(root, f, pattern, hits)
        end
      end
    elseif vim.fn.filereadable(root) == 1 then
      scan_file(vim.fs.dirname(root), root, pattern, hits)
    end
  end

  return hits
end

nodes.name: source.lua
nodes.summary: The third drift axis: what this config's **source** actually registers, as extracted by docmap.nvim's `core/bindings.lua` and already baked into…
nodes.body:
`drift.lua` compared two axes: *documented* (the BINDINGS cheatsheets,
via `records.lua`) against *live* (`nvim_get_keymap`/`nvim_get_commands`).
This adds the third, and it is specifically what makes the missing
direction possible.

**Why "live-but-undocumented" was never built, and why source fixes it.**
`drift.lua`'s own limitation 1 says the reverse check would mean diffing
against EVERY global keymap — vim's own defaults, matchit, every
plugin's own bindings — flooding the report with things this corpus was
never meant to document. That objection is entirely about the *live*
axis. The source axis has no such problem by construction: it only ever
contains registrations written in **this repository's own Lua**, which
is exactly the set the Personal cheatsheets are supposed to cover. So
"in the source, not in the docs" is a clean, bounded question that
"live, not in the docs" could never be.

**Reads the artifact, does not scan.** `docs/map/module_map.json` is
already generated and committed, and docmap.nvim's whole posture
is that its artifacts are cold-readable without a live session. A scan
here would re-parse ~500 files to re-derive data sitting on disk.

The cost of that choice, stated rather than hidden: the artifact is only
as fresh as the last `:DocMap`. A binding added since then is missing
from this axis, which reads as "documented but not in source" — the
opposite of the truth. Hence `M.generated_at`, and hence every finding
from this axis naming the artifact rather than claiming to have read the
source itself.

Nothing here requires docmap.nvim to be loaded, or installed: it
reads a JSON file. If the file is absent, or predates the bindings
extractor, that is reported as a reason, never as "no bindings found".

function M.load()
  local path = map_path()
  local stat = vim.uv.fs_stat(path)
  if not stat then
    return nil, ("no map artifact at %s — run :DocMap in this config first"):format(path), nil
  end

  local fd = io.open(path, "rb")
  if not fd then
    return nil, ("cannot read %s"):format(path), nil

nodes.body:
Deliberately does NOT run the drift check. That takes ~650ms across four
axes and produces a report, which is what `:Bindings check` and
`:Bindings report` are for; a dashboard that made you wait would be opened
once. Everything here is either a cheap live API call or one pass over the
corpus, and the drift line only reports what the last written report says
— the file, not a fresh measurement.

The route list at the bottom exists because it is the honest answer to the
most common reason for typing `:Bindings` at all: the verb tree has grown
past what a `desc` string shows in completion, and this is the `?`-style
cheatsheet the roadmap point asked for.

User-facing output is German, deliberately and consistently across every
string of `:Bindings` (see the note in init.lua).

local function md_count(root, category, skip)
  local dir = vim.fs.joinpath(root, category)
  if vim.fn.isdirectory(dir) ~= 1 then
    return 0
  end
  local n = 0
  for _, f in ipairs(collect_recursive.files(dir)) do
    if f:match("%.md$") and not (skip and skip[vim.fn.fnamemodify(f, ":t:r")]) then
      n = n + 1
    end
  end
  return n
end

local function corpus()
  -- Since 2026-09-04 the corpus has three origins, not two: the two cheatsheet
  -- roots and the personal plugins' own `docs/BINDINGS.md`. Counting by
  -- `rec.scope` worked while "Personal" meant exactly one root -- a repo sheet
  -- carries the same scope and would be silently added to the cheatsheet
  -- block, putting a row count next to a file count that didn't produce it.
  -- So the path decides here, not the field.
  local sheets = config.plugin_sheets() or {}
  local is_plugin_sheet, superseded = {}, {}
  for _, sheet in ipairs(sheets) do
    is_plugin_sheet[vim.fs.normalize(sheet.file)] = true
    superseded[sheet.plugin] = true
    superseded[(sheet.plugin:gsub("%.nvim$", ""))] = true
  end

  local rows, meta_rows, files_with_rows = {}, 0, {}
  for _, rec in ipairs(records.list()) do
    local origin = is_plugin_sheet[vim.fs.normalize(rec.file)] and "Plugin" or rec.scope
    local key = origin .. "/" .. rec.category
    rows[key] = (rows[key] or 0) + 1
    files_with_rows[rec.file] = true
    if rec.meta then
      meta_rows = meta_rows + 1
    end
  end

  local scopes = {}
  for idx, root in ipairs(config.roots()) do
    local scope = idx == 1 and "Personal" or "Extern"
    local cats = {}
    for _, cat in ipairs(CATEGORIES) do
      cats[#cats + 1] = {
        name = cat,
        -- Only the Personal root has superseded sheets; the Extern root
        -- documents third-party plugins that ship no `docs/BINDINGS.md`.
        files = md_count(root, cat, idx == 1 and superseded or nil),
        rows = rows[scope .. "/" .. cat] or 0,
      }
    end
    scopes[#scopes + 1] = { name = scope, root = root, categories = cats }

local function live()
  local global_by_mode, global_total, buf_total = {}, 0, 0
  for _, mode in ipairs(MODES) do
    local n = #vim.api.nvim_get_keymap(mode)
    if n > 0 then
      global_by_mode[#global_by_mode + 1] = ("%s %d"):format(mode, n)
    end
    global_total = global_total + n
    for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
      if vim.api.nvim_buf_is_loaded(buf) then
        buf_total = buf_total + #vim.api.nvim_buf_get_keymap(buf, mode)
      end
    end
  end

  local groups, autocmds = {}, {}
  local ok, list = pcall(vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds, {})
  if ok then
    autocmds = list
    for _, au in ipairs(list) do
      if au.group_name then
        groups[au.group_name] = true
      end
    end
  end

  return {
    keymaps_global = global_total,
    keymaps_by_mode = table.concat(global_by_mode, ", "),
    keymaps_buffer = buf_total,
    usercmds = vim.tbl_count(vim.api.nvim_get_commands({})),
    autocmds = #autocmds,
    autocmd_groups = vim.tbl_count(groups),
  }
end

nodes.name: cdx
nodes.summary: The templates live in `docs/NOTES/CDX/templates/PROMPT/` of this config and are pasted into Claude Code by hand all day, so this saves the detour through a…
nodes.body:
:Cdx prompt <name> [sha ...]
  :Cdx open prompt <name>

`:Cdx open prompt <name>` does not copy anything but opens the template
file itself in the current window (`:edit`), to change it; the name is
resolved like for `:Cdx prompt`, SHAs do not apply. `:Cdx open` is the
place for further things to open.

`<name>` is every `*.md` file of that folder, without the extension
(`Base`, `full`, `review_w_ultracode`, `ultra_sha`, a new file the moment it
is saved), and completes with `<Tab>`; the folder is read on every
completion and every call, so nothing has to be registered. The matching is
case-insensitive, and two short names stay for the two that were there first
(a file of that very name wins: `review.md` is used before the short name `review`):

  base    Base.md
  review  review_w_ultracode.md

A template that contains `{SHA}` takes any number of commit SHAs, as
separate arguments, as one comma-separated token (`abc1234,def5678`), or as
a quoted string (`"abc1234, def5678"`) -- all of them end up as
`abc1234, def5678` in the text. Without a SHA the template is copied
unchanged, `{SHA}` included; arguments for a template without the
placeholder are ignored with a warning.

The template directory is read from `stdpath("config")`, not from the
repository the current window happens to be in, so the command works from
any project. The copy goes through `lib.nvim.cross.copy_to_clipboard`
(Windows, macOS, Linux X11/Wayland, WSL).

functions.snippet:
local function list_templates()
  local by_stem, stems = {}, {}
  local handle = vim.uv.fs_scandir(prompt_dir())
  while handle do
    local name, kind = vim.uv.fs_scandir_next(handle)
    if not name then
      break
    end
    local stem = name:match("^(.+)%.md$")
    if stem and kind ~= "directory" then
      by_stem[stem] = name
      stems[#stems + 1] = stem
    end
  end
  table.sort(stems)
  return by_stem, stems
end
functions.summary: Every template of the folder: the file stem -> the file name.

function M.resolve(typed)
  local by_stem, stems = list_templates()
  if by_stem[typed] then
    return by_stem[typed], nil
  end
  for _, stem in ipairs(stems) do
    if stem:lower() == typed:lower() then
      return by_stem[stem], nil
    end
  end
  local alias = ALIASES[typed:lower()]
  if alias and vim.tbl_contains(vim.tbl_values(by_stem), alias) then
    return alias, nil
  end
  return nil,
    ("no prompt template '%s' in %s (have: %s)"):format(
      typed,
      prompt_dir(),
      table.concat(stems, ", ")
    )
end

function M.names()
  local by_stem, stems = list_templates()
  local files = vim.tbl_values(by_stem)
  local out = vim.list_extend({}, stems)
  for alias, file in pairs(ALIASES) do
    -- `base` for `Base.md` is the stem in another case: offering both says the same word twice
    local is_stem_in_other_case = false
    for _, stem in ipairs(stems) do
      if stem:lower() == alias then
        is_stem_in_other_case = true
      end
    end
    if vim.tbl_contains(files, file) and not is_stem_in_other_case then
      out[#out + 1] = alias
    end
  end
  table.sort(out)
  return out
end

  local fh, open_err = io.open(path, "rb")
  if not fh then
    return nil, ("cannot read %s: %s"):format(path, open_err or "unknown error")
  end
  local text = fh:read("*a")
  fh:close()
  -- Strip a leading blank line (in case a template ever has one) and CRLF
  -- endings from Windows; neither belongs in the pasted prompt.
  text = text:gsub("\r\n", "\n"):gsub("^%s*\n", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
  return text, nil
end

functions.name: M.parse_shas
functions.snippet:
function M.parse_shas(tokens)
  local shas = {}
  for _, token in ipairs(tokens) do
    for piece in token:gmatch("[^,%s\"']+") do
      -- Git accepts abbreviations down to 4 hex digits; a full SHA-1 has 40
      -- (SHA-256 repositories 64). Anything else is a typo, and copying it
      -- would only surface once the prompt has been pasted and run.
      if not (piece:match("^%x+$") and #piece >= 4 and #piece <= 64) then
        return nil, ("not a commit SHA: %q"):format(piece)
      end
      shas[#shas + 1] = piece
    end
  end
  return shas, nil
end
functions.summary: Turn whatever the user typed after the template name into a list of SHAs: tokens may themselves contain commas, so `a,b c` and `"a, b" c` are three SHAs.

functions.name: copy
functions.snippet:
local function copy(text, label)
  if not copy_to_clipboard(text) then
    notify.error("Could not write to the clipboard")
    return false
  end
  notify.info(("Copied %s (%d chars)"):format(label, vim.fn.strchars(text)))

functions.name: M.copy_prompt
functions.snippet:
function M.copy_prompt(typed, tokens)
  local file, rerr = M.resolve(typed)
  if not file then
    notify.error(rerr or "unknown prompt template")
    return false
  end
  local text, err = read_template(file)
  if not text then
    notify.error(err or "template not readable")
    return false
  end
  local has_placeholder = text:find(SHA_PLACEHOLDER, 1, true) ~= nil
  if #tokens == 0 then
    return copy(text, file)
  end
  if not has_placeholder then
    notify.warn(
      ("%s has no %s placeholder; the arguments are ignored"):format(file, SHA_PLACEHOLDER)
    )
    return copy(text, file)
  end
  local shas, perr = M.parse_shas(tokens)
  if not shas then
    notify.error(perr or "invalid SHA")
    return false
  end
  -- Function replacement: the SHA list is data, `%` in it must not be read as
  -- a capture reference.
  local filled = text:gsub(vim.pesc(SHA_PLACEHOLDER), function()
    return table.concat(shas, SHA_JOIN)
  end)
  return copy(filled, ("%s (%d SHA)"):format(file, #shas))
end
functions.summary: Copy a template; `tokens` (SHAs) replace `{SHA}` when it has the placeholder and there are any.

functions.name: M.open_prompt
functions.snippet:
function M.open_prompt(typed)
  local file, rerr = M.resolve(typed)
  if not file then
    notify.error(rerr or "unknown prompt template")
    return false
  end
  local path = vim.fs.joinpath(prompt_dir(), file)
  -- Fails in a 'winfixbuf' window (E1513) or with 'nohidden' over a modified buffer (E37).
  local opened, oerr = pcall(vim.cmd.edit, vim.fn.fnameescape(path))
  if not opened then
    notify.error(("Could not open %s: %s"):format(path, tostring(oerr)))
    return false
  end
  return true
end

nodes.name: clipboard
nodes.summary: The report and handover folders under `docs/ROADMAP/` are pasted into Claude Code prompts, shells and file dialogs all day, so this saves the detour through a…
nodes.body:
:Clipboard path reports      <config>/docs/ROADMAP/reports
  :Clipboard path handovers    <config>/docs/ROADMAP/handovers

`path` is the first sub-command of `:Clipboard`: further things to copy
(a file's content, a link, ...) get their own word next to it later, which
is why the directory targets sit one level down. `path` itself is
optional -- `:Clipboard reports` is the same as `:Clipboard path reports`.

Snippets are the second kind of target: a fixed text (usually an Ex command that is
tedious to type) that is copied verbatim, no path involved:

  :Clipboard remove citeX      :%s/\[cite: \d\+\]//g   (strips "[cite: 12]" markers)

They live in `M.SNIPPETS` (words -> text), extendable through `enable({ snippets = ... })`.

Deliberately no keymap (`<leader>cf` / `cg` belong to casedesk.nvim).

The path is copied as an absolute path with forward slashes -- directly
usable in a shell, an explorer address bar and Neovim alike. With
`form = "env"` it is folded into `$NVIM_CONFIG_DIR/...` (or whatever root
gopath.nvim's `shorten_path` knows) when the directory lies under one; a
directory under no known root stays absolute.

Targets are plain data (`M.TARGETS`, name -> directory relative to
`stdpath("config")`, or absolute, `$ENV` allowed): `enable({ targets = {
notes = "docs/NOTES" } })` adds more `:Clipboard` arguments without touching
this file. The copy goes through `lib.nvim.cross.copy_to_clipboard`
(Windows, macOS, Linux X11/Wayland, WSL).

local function is_absolute(dir)
  return dir:match("^%a:[/\\]") ~= nil or dir:sub(1, 1) == "/" or dir:sub(1, 1) == "~"
end

function M.resolve(dir)
  local expanded = expand_path(dir)
  if not is_absolute(expanded) then
    expanded = vim.fs.joinpath(vim.fn.stdpath("config"), expanded)
  end
  return (vim.fs.normalize(expanded):gsub("/+$", ""))
end

functions.name: M.format
functions.snippet:
function M.format(path)
  if settings.form ~= "env" then
    return path
  end
  local ok, gopath = pcall(require, "gopath.env_shorten")
  if ok and type(gopath.shorten_path) == "function" then
    local shortened = gopath.shorten_path(path)
    if shortened then
      return shortened
    end
  end
  local cfg = (vim.fs.normalize(vim.fn.stdpath("config")):gsub("/+$", ""))
  -- Case-insensitive only where the file system is (Windows).
  local fold = vim.fn.has("win32") == 1 and string.lower or function(s)
    return s
  end
  if fold(path) == fold(cfg) then
    return "$NVIM_CONFIG_DIR"
  end
  if fold(path:sub(1, #cfg + 1)) == fold(cfg .. "/") then
    return "$NVIM_CONFIG_DIR" .. path:sub(#cfg + 1)
  end
  return path
end

functions.name: shorten_for_echo
functions.snippet:
local function shorten_for_echo(text)
  local max = math.max(20, vim.o.columns - 30)
  if vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(text) <= max then
    return text
  end
  local chars = vim.fn.strchars(text)
  local lo, hi = 1, chars
  while lo < hi do
    local mid = math.ceil((lo + hi) / 2)
    if vim.fn.strdisplaywidth(vim.fn.strcharpart(text, chars - mid)) <= max - 1 then
      lo = mid
    else
      hi = mid - 1
    end
  end
  return "…" .. vim.fn.strcharpart(text, chars - lo)
end
functions.summary: Shorten `text` for a one-line status message: past the editor width minus room for the prefix only the tail is kept, behind an ellipsis.

function M.copy(name)
  local dir = M.TARGETS[name]
  if not dir then
    notify.error(("unknown target %q (known: %s)"):format(name, table.concat(M.names(), ", ")))
    return false
  end

  local path = M.resolve(dir)
  if vim.fn.isdirectory(path) == 0 then
    notify.error(("directory does not exist: %s"):format(path))
    return false
  end

  local text = M.format(path)
  if not copy_to_clipboard(text) then
    notify.warn(("no clipboard provider accepted %s"):format(shorten_for_echo(text)))
    return false
  end
  notify.info(("copied %s -> %s"):format(name, shorten_for_echo(text)))
  return true
end

function M.enable(opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  if type(opts.targets) == "table" then
    for name, dir in pairs(opts.targets) do
      if type(name) == "string" and type(dir) == "string" then
        M.TARGETS[name] = dir
      end
    end
  end
  if type(opts.snippets) == "table" then
    for key, snippet in pairs(opts.snippets) do
      if type(key) == "string" and type(snippet) == "table" and type(snippet.text) == "string" then
        local words = snippet_words(key)
        if #words == 0 then
          -- An empty path would register a ROOT route and hijack a bare `:Clipboard`.
          notify.warn(("ignoring snippet with an empty key (%q)"):format(key))
        else
          M.SNIPPETS[table.concat(words, " ")] = {
            text = snippet.text,
            desc = type(snippet.desc) == "string" and snippet.desc or "Copy a snippet",
          }
        end

    end
  end
  if opts.form == "absolute" or opts.form == "env" then

  local taken = {}
  for _, name in ipairs(M.names()) do
    taken[name] = true
    taken["path " .. name] = true
    local function run()
      M.copy(name)
    end
    local desc = ("Copy the path of %s"):format(M.TARGETS[name])

nodes.name: context_open
nodes.summary: `M-o` / `M-O` / `:ContextOpen` -- one dispatcher unifying "open the thing under the cursor" across gopath.nvim (gF), markdown.nvim (TableView), images.nvim,…
nodes.body:
See README.md for the full design and an extension guide.

`M.open()`  (M-o, bare `:ContextOpen`): resolve every provider
(`context_open.providers`) against the cursor position. Zero matches ->
search the rest of the current line instead (`context_open.scan`). Zero
candidates either way -> notify. One -> run it directly. More than one ->
`lib.nvim.ui.kit.select` ("Open with…"), the same ambiguity-picker
pattern open.nvim's own `open.picker` uses.

`M.list()`  (M-O, `:ContextOpen list`): every openable target in the
whole buffer (`context_open.scan.buffer_targets`), picked from one list;
selecting an entry jumps the cursor to it and runs its action.

functions.name: notify
resolve_candidates
functions.snippet:
local function resolve_candidates(candidates, empty_msg)
  if #candidates == 0 then
    notify().warn(empty_msg)
    return
  end
  if #candidates == 1 then
    candidates[1].run()
    return
  end
  require("lib.nvim.ui.kit").select({
    title = "Open with…",
    items = candidates,
    respect_override = true,
    format_item = function(c)
      return c.label
    end,
    on_select = function(c)
      if c then
        c.run()
      end
    end,
  })
end
functions.summary: Show `candidates` and act on the choice: run the sole candidate directly, prompt when there is more than one, notify `empty_msg` when there are none.

functions.name: M.open
functions.snippet:
function M.open()
  local ok_ctx, context = pcall(function()
    require("bindings.usrcmds.context_open.util").ensure_loaded("open.nvim")
    return require("open.context")
  end)
  if not ok_ctx then
    notify().error("open.nvim unavailable")
    return
  end

  local signals = context.gather()
  local candidates = providers.collect(signals)

  if #candidates > 0 then
    resolve_candidates(candidates, "Nothing to open here")
    return
  end

  -- Nothing directly under the cursor: fall back to scanning the rest of
  -- the line for something openable.
  local lnum = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]
  resolve_candidates(scan.line_targets(lnum), "Nothing to open on this line")
end
functions.summary: Open whatever is under the cursor.

functions.name: M.list
functions.snippet:
function M.list()
  local candidates = scan.buffer_targets()
  if #candidates == 0 then
    notify().warn("No openable targets found in this buffer")
    return
  end

  require("lib.nvim.ui.kit").select({
    title = ("Open — buffer targets (%d)"):format(#candidates),
    items = candidates,
    respect_override = true,
    format_item = function(c)
      return c.label
    end,
    on_select = function(c)
      if not c then
        return
      end
      if c.lnum then
        pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, 0, { c.lnum, c.col or 0 })
      end
      c.run()
    end,
  })
end
functions.summary: List every openable target in the buffer.

local function owned_extension(path)
  if not path then
    return false
  end
  local ext = path:match("%.([%w]+)$")
  if not ext then
    return false
  end
  ext = ext:lower()
  if ext == "pdf" then
    return true
  end
  local ok, images_cfg = pcall(function()
    return require("images.config").get()
  end)
  if ok and images_cfg.extensions then
    for _, e in ipairs(images_cfg.extensions) do
      if e:lower() == ext then
        return true
      end
    end
  end
  return false
end

functions.name: M.open_nvim
functions.snippet:
function M.open_nvim(signals)
  if not has_open_target(signals) then
    return {}
  end

  util.ensure_loaded("open.nvim")
  local ok_ctx, context = pcall(require, "open.context")
  local ok_reg, registry = pcall(require, "open.registry")
  if not (ok_ctx and ok_reg) then
    return {}
  end

  if owned_extension(signals.cfile_path) then
    return {}
  end

  local out = {}
  for _, key in ipairs(context.candidate_targets(signals)) do
    local handler = registry.get(key)
    if handler then
      out[#out + 1] = {
        label = ("open: %s — %s"):format(key, handler.desc),
        run = function()
          local ctx = context.resolve(nil, key, signals)
          if ctx then
            registry.dispatch(key, ctx)
          end
        end,
      }
    end
  end
  return out
end

local function pdf_path_under_cursor(signals)
  local candidate = signals.cfile_path or signals.cfile
  if not candidate or candidate == "" then
    return nil
  end
  -- `expand_path`, not `vim.fn.expand()`: this string is whatever happens to
  -- sit under the cursor in someone else's buffer. `vim.fn.expand()` is
  -- filename expansion, so a backtick span in it is a command substitution
  -- run through 'shell', and `%`/`#`/`<cfile>` are Vim specials that silently
  -- resolve to other paths. Only `~` and environment variables are wanted.
  local abs = vim.fn.fnamemodify(require("lib.nvim.cross.fs.expand_path")(candidate), ":p")
  if not abs:lower():match("%.pdf$") then
    return nil
  end
  if vim.uv.fs_stat(abs) then
    return abs
  end
  return nil
end

function M.collect(signals)
  local out = {}
  for _, provider in ipairs(M.ORDER) do

    if ok and candidates then

local function table_candidates(bufnr)
  local ft = vim.bo[bufnr].filetype
  if ft ~= "markdown" and ft ~= "mdx" and ft ~= "md" then
    return {}
  end

  local ok, parser = pcall(require, "markdown.tableview.parser")
  if not ok then
    return {}
  end

  local out = {}
  for _, tbl in ipairs(parser.get_tables(bufnr)) do
    out[#out + 1] = {
      label = ("%d: table  toggle table view (%d row(s))"):format(
        tbl.start_line,
        #(tbl.rows or {})
      ),
      lnum = tbl.start_line,
      col = 0,
      run = function()
        vim.cmd("TableViewToggle")
      end,
    }
  end
  return out
end

returns.desc: nil when the line doesn't look like an import at all

functions.snippet:
local function import_target_col(line)
  for _, pat in ipairs(IMPORT_PATTERNS) do
    local s, e = line:find(pat)
    if s then
      local quote = line:find("[\"'<]", s)
      if quote then
        return quote
      end
      local rest = line:sub(e + 1)
      local ws = rest:match("^%s*") or ""
      return e + #ws
    end
  end
  return nil
end

functions.name: gopath_import_candidates
functions.snippet:
local function gopath_import_candidates(bufnr)
  if bufnr ~= vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() then
    return {} -- resolve_at_cursor only ever sees the current window/buffer
  end
  local ok_gopath, gopath = pcall(require, "gopath")
  if not ok_gopath then
    return {}
  end

  local win = vim.api.nvim_get_current_win()
  local original = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(win)
  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, 0, -1, false)

  local out = {}
  for lnum, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local col = import_target_col(line)
    if col then
      if pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, win, { lnum, col }) then
        local ok_res, res = pcall(gopath.resolve)
        -- `exists == false` is gopath's own last-resort "raw cfile, nothing
        -- actually found" fallback (see gopath.resolve's step 6) -- not
        -- worth surfacing as an openable target.
        if ok_res and res and res.exists ~= false then
          out[#out + 1] = {
            label = ("%d: gopath  %s"):format(lnum, res.path or res.subject or "?"),
            lnum = lnum,
            col = col,
            run = function()
              gopath.commands.resolve_and_open("edit")
            end,
          }
        end
      end
    end
  end

  pcall(vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor, win, original)
  return out
end

functions.name: M.buffer_targets
functions.snippet:
function M.buffer_targets(bufnr)
  bufnr = bufnr or vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  util.ensure_loaded("open.nvim")

  local out = {}
  local ok, viewer_scan = pcall(require, "open.viewer.scan")
  if ok then
    local links =
      viewer_scan.from_source(source_for_buffer(bufnr), { paths = true, code_fences = true })
    for _, lk in ipairs(links) do
      out[#out + 1] = candidate_from_link(lk)
    end
  end

  vim.list_extend(out, table_candidates(bufnr))
  vim.list_extend(out, gopath_import_candidates(bufnr))

  table.sort(out, function(a, b)
    return (a.lnum or 0) < (b.lnum or 0)
  end)
  return out
end

function M.line_targets(lnum)
  util.ensure_loaded("open.nvim")
  local ok, viewer_scan = pcall(require, "open.viewer.scan")
  if not ok then
    return {}
  end

  local line = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, lnum - 1, lnum, false)[1] or ""
  local base_dir = vim.fn.expand("%:p:h")
  local links = viewer_scan.from_line(line, lnum, { paths = true, base_dir = base_dir })

  local out = {}
  for _, lk in ipairs(links) do
    out[#out + 1] = candidate_from_link(lk)
  end
  return out
end

nodes.name: util.lua
nodes.summary: Small shared helper: force-load a lazy.nvim plugin spec that is `cmd`-gated (not `ft`/`event`-gated), so a provider's very first invocation in a session still…
nodes.body:
`open.nvim` and `pdfport.nvim` are both `cmd`-only in plugins/personal/specs/navigate.lua; calling e.g. `require("open.context")` before `:Open` has ever run would otherwise fail with "module not found".

Cheap and idempotent: `lazy.core.loader.load` checks `plugin._.loaded`
itself and no-ops when the plugin is already on the runtime path (the
common case -- gopath.nvim/markdown.nvim/images.nvim are already loaded
via `event`/`ft` by the time a keymap can fire).

function M.ensure_loaded(plugin_name)
  local ok, loader = pcall(require, "lazy.core.loader")
  if not ok then
    return
  end
  pcall(loader.load, plugin_name, { source = "context_open" })
end

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Text in a buffer is often a command: a note that says `` `:set wrap` ``, a README block with `git status`, a line of Lua.
nodes.body:
`:Execute` takes that text, works out what it is and runs it, shows it in the command line first, or copies it.

  :Execute [how] [--from=<where>] [--as=<kind>] [--yes]       (with a range: the selected text)
  :Execute! [how] ...                                         (the bang runs it at once)

`how` (what happens, `<Tab>` completes it; default `cmdline`, with a bang `run`):

  cmdline    type it into the command line, do not run it: edit it, press <CR>
  run        run it, show the output as a message
  split | vsplit | tab | float    run it, show the output in a scratch buffer / floating window
  clipboard  copy the command text, do not run it
  result     run it, copy the output to the + register

`--from` (the text): `auto` (the default: selection, else the `code` span under the cursor, else the
fenced block, else the line), `selection`, `backtick`, `line`, `fence`, `clipboard`.

`--as` (the kind): `auto` (the default), `ex`, `lua`, `shell`. `auto` reads the fence language or the first
character: `!cmd` and `$ cmd` are shell, `:cmd` is Ex, the rest is Ex.

Shell commands, an Ex shell filter (`:r !`, `:%!`, `:terminal`) and Lua that names a shell entry point
ask `[R]un / [C]ancel` before they run; `--yes` skips the question. `cmdline` and `clipboard` never run
anything.

Mappings (`bindings.mappings.execute`): `<leader>x` is `:Execute`, `<leader>X` is `:Execute!`, in Normal and
Visual mode.

Key responsibilities:
 - `execute`: the whole flow for one invocation (`source` -> `kind` -> `sink`), callable from Lua
 - `enable`: registers the `:Execute` verb with the composer from lib.nvim

Not its job: finding the text (`execute.source`), classifying it (`execute.kind`), running it and
showing the result (`execute.sink`).

function M.execute(opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  local src, serr = source.get({ from = opts.from, range = opts.range })
  if not src then
    notify.warn(serr or "nothing to execute")
    return
  end
  local plan, perr = kind.build(src.lines, opts.as, src.lang)
  if not plan then
    notify.warn(perr or "nothing to execute")
    return
  end
  local how = opts.how or M.default_how(opts.bang)

  ---Run the plan and show the result in the way `how` says (after the question, when the plan leaves the editor).
  ---@param run_how Execute.How
  local function run(run_how)
    if plan.risky and not opts.yes then
      M.confirm(plan, function(accepted)
        if not accepted then
          notify.info("Cancelled")
          return
        end
        sink.run(plan, function(res)
          sink.deliver(run_how, res, plan)
        end)
      end)
      return
    end
    sink.run(plan, function(res)
      sink.deliver(run_how, res, plan)
    end)
  end

  if how == "cmdline" then
    local text, terr = kind.cmdline_text(plan)
    if not text then
      -- the plan is known and shown: run it, copy it, or leave it (Cancel is the default)
      M.offer(plan, terr or "cannot put it into the command line", function(choice)
        if choice == "copy" then

nodes.name: kind.lua
nodes.summary: `:Execute` takes any text.
nodes.body:
This module turns it into a `Execute.Plan`: the kind, the individual commands with their markers stripped, a display form, and a `risky` flag.

Kind detection (`as = "auto"`), first match wins:
  1. the language of a fenced block: bash / sh / zsh / shell / console / pwsh / powershell / cmd / bat
     are shell, lua is Lua, vim / vimscript / ex are Ex
  2. the first character of the first line: `!` or `$ ` is shell, `:` is Ex
  3. otherwise Ex

A leading `:` / `!` / `$ ` is only a marker (`` `:set wrap` ``, `` `!git status` ``, `$ git status`), it is
removed before anything runs. `as` pins the kind and skips the detection.

`risky` is true for what reaches outside the editor: every shell command, an Ex command that is a
shell filter or `:terminal`, and a Lua chunk that names an obvious shell entry point. The command asks
before it runs such a plan. Ex and Lua are otherwise not guarded: they are what the user could type in
the command line, and the default of `:Execute` (without a bang) shows them there first.

Not its job: finding the text (`execute.source`), running it (`execute.sink`).

functions.name: first_text
functions.snippet:
local function first_text(lines)
  for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local trimmed = vim.trim(line)
    if trimmed ~= "" then
      return trimmed
    end
  end
  return nil
end
functions.summary: The first line that has text.

functions.name: M.detect
functions.snippet:
function M.detect(lines, lang)
  if lang and LANG_KIND[lang] then
    return LANG_KIND[lang]
  end
  local first = first_text(lines)
  if first then
    if first:sub(1, 1) == "!" or first:match("^%$%s") then
      return "shell"
    end
  end
  return "ex"
end
functions.summary: Decide the kind of `lines` when the user did not say.

functions.name: unmark
functions.snippet:
local function unmark(line, kind)
  if kind == "shell" then
    return (line:gsub("^!%s*", ""):gsub("^%$%s+", ""))
  elseif kind == "ex" then
    return (line:gsub("^:+%s*", ""))
  end
  return line
end
functions.summary: Strip the marker a kind may carry from one line.

functions.name: ex_commands
functions.snippet:
local function ex_commands(lines)
  local out = {}
  for _, raw in ipairs(lines) do
    local line = vim.trim(raw)
    if line:sub(1, 1) == "\\" and #out > 0 then
      -- Vim keeps what follows the backslash as written (`\ wrap` adds " wrap"), only the indent before it goes
      out[#out] = out[#out] .. line:sub(2)
    elseif line ~= "" and line:sub(1, 1) ~= '"' then
      out[#out + 1] = unmark(line, "ex")
    end
  end
  return out
end
functions.summary: Ex commands of `lines`: one per entry.

functions.name: shell_commands
functions.snippet:
local function shell_commands(lines, strip_bang)
  local out = {}
  local pending
  local function add(line)
    if #out > 0 or not strip_bang then
      -- only the "$ " prompt is a marker here
      out[#out + 1] = (line:gsub("^%$%s+", ""))
    else
      out[#out + 1] = unmark(line, "shell")
    end
  end
  for _, raw in ipairs(lines) do
    local line = vim.trim(raw)
    if pending then
      line = pending .. " " .. line
      pending = nil
    end
    if line:match("%s\\$") then
      pending = vim.trim(line:sub(1, -2))
    elseif line ~= "" and line:sub(1, 1) ~= "#" then
      add(line)
    end
  end
  if pending and pending ~= "" then
    add(pending)
  end
  return out
end
functions.summary: Shell command lines of `lines`: one per entry.

functions.name: abbrev
functions.snippet:
local function abbrev(name, full, min)
  return #name >= min and #name <= #full and full:sub(1, #name) == name
end
functions.summary: Whether `name` is `full` or an abbreviation of it that Vim accepts (at least `min` letters).

functions.name: in_list
functions.snippet:
local function in_list(name, list)
  for _, entry in ipairs(list) do
    if abbrev(name, entry[1], entry[2]) then
      return true
    end
  end
  return false
end

functions.name: split_bars
functions.snippet:
local function split_bars(cmd)
  local parts, start = {}, 1
  for i = 1, #cmd do
    local c = cmd:sub(i, i)
    local before = i > 1 and cmd:sub(i - 1, i - 1) or ""
    if c == "|" and before ~= "\\" and before ~= "\22" then
      parts[#parts + 1] = cmd:sub(start, i - 1)
      start = i + 1
    end
  end
  parts[#parts + 1] = cmd:sub(start)
  return parts
end
functions.summary: Split a command line at the bars that join commands (`set wrap | !ls`).

functions.name: strip_range
functions.snippet:
local function strip_range(text)
  local s = text
  while true do
    local before = s
    s = s:gsub("^%s+", "")
    s = s:gsub("^[%d%.%$%%,;%+%-]+", "")
    s = s:gsub("^'[%w<>%[%]'`\"%^%.]", "")
    s = s:gsub("^/[^/]*/?", "")
    s = s:gsub("^%?[^?]*%??", "")
    if s == before then
      return s
    end
  end
end
functions.summary: Remove the range in front of a command name: numbers, `.`, `$`, `%`, marks (`'a`, `'<`), patterns (`/foo/`, `?foo?`), offsets and the separators `,` and `;`.

functions.name: part_is_risky
functions.snippet:
local function part_is_risky(part, depth)
  if depth > 8 then
    return true -- nested deeper than anything sensible: ask
  end
  local rest = strip_range(part)
  if rest:sub(1, 1) == "!" then
    return true
  end
  local name = rest:match("^(%a+)")
  if not name then
    return false
  end
  local after = rest:sub(#name + 1)

  -- modifiers and repeaters: the command behind them is what counts
  if in_list(name, MODIFIERS) or in_list(name, REPEATERS) then
    after = after:gsub("^!", "")
    return part_is_risky(after, depth + 1)
  end
  if name == "g" or name == "global" or name == "v" or name == "vglobal" then
    -- :g/pattern/command, with any delimiter
    local delim = after:gsub("^!", ""):sub(1, 1)
    if delim == "" then
      return false
    end
    local cmd = after:gsub("^!", ""):match(
      "^" .. vim.pesc(delim) .. "[^" .. vim.pesc(delim) .. "]*" .. vim.pesc(delim) .. "(.*)$"
    )
    return cmd ~= nil and part_is_risky(cmd, depth + 1)
  end

  if abbrev(name, "read", 1) then
    return after:match("^%s*!") ~= nil
  end
  if abbrev(name, "write", 1) or abbrev(name, "wall", 2) then
    -- ":w !cmd" pipes the buffer into a command; ":w! file" is a forced write
    return after:match("^%s+!") ~= nil
  end
  if in_list(name, EXTERNALS) then
    return true

      return true

params.desc: fence language, used by the detection
params.name: lang

functions.snippet:
function M.build(lines, as, lang)
  as = as or "auto"
  local kind = as == "auto" and M.detect(lines, lang) or as
  ---@cast kind Execute.Kind

  if kind == "lua" then
    local chunk = vim.trim(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
    if not chunk:find("\n", 1, true) then
      chunk = chunk:gsub("^:?lua%s+", "")
    end
    if chunk == "" then
      return nil, "nothing to run: the text is empty"
    end
    return {
      kind = "lua",
      commands = { chunk },
      display = "lua: " .. chunk,
      risky = M.lua_is_risky(chunk),
    },
      nil
  end

  local commands = kind == "shell"
      and shell_commands(lines, not (lang and LANG_KIND[lang] == "shell"))
    or ex_commands(lines)
  if #commands == 0 then
    return nil, "nothing to run: the text is empty (or only comments)"
  end
  local prefix = kind == "shell" and "!" or ":"
  local shown, risky = {}, kind == "shell"
  for i, cmd in ipairs(commands) do
    shown[i] = prefix .. cmd
    if kind == "ex" and M.ex_is_risky(cmd) then
      risky = true
    end
  end
  return {
    kind = kind,
    commands = commands,
    display = table.concat(shown, "\n"),
functions.summary: Build the plan for a piece of text.

functions.name: M.cmdline_text
functions.snippet:
function M.cmdline_text(plan)
  if plan.kind == "lua" then
    local chunk = plan.commands[1]
    if chunk:find("\n", 1, true) then
      return nil, "a Lua chunk with several lines does not fit the command line"
    end
    return "lua " .. chunk, nil
  end
  if #plan.commands > 1 then
    return nil, ("%d commands do not fit the command line"):format(#plan.commands)
  end
  return (plan.kind == "shell" and "!" or "") .. plan.commands[1], nil
end

nodes.name: sink.lua
nodes.summary: Two steps, kept apart so a spec can drive each one:
nodes.body:
`run(plan, cb)`        executes the plan and calls `cb` once with an `Execute.Result`
  `deliver(how, ...)`    shows / copies the result

How each kind runs:
  ex     every command through `nvim_exec2(..., { output = true })`, in the window that was current, so
         `:set wrap` or `:echo expand("%")` act on the buffer the text came from. Stops at the first error.
  lua    the chunk is tried as an expression first (`vim.o.shiftwidth` shows its value), else as
         statements. `print` is captured. A returned value is appended through `vim.inspect`.
  shell  every command line through `vim.fn.jobstart` with a command string, which uses 'shell' and
         'shellcmdflag' like `:!` does (so quoting is the shell's own). Asynchronous, one command after
         the other, stops at the first non-zero exit.

Where the result goes (`how`):
  cmdline / clipboard   not run: the command is typed into the command line / copied
  run                   run, then show the output as a message
  split / vsplit / tab  run, then show the output in a scratch buffer of that kind
  float                 run, then show the output in a floating viewer
  result                run, then copy the output to the + register

Not its job: finding the text (`execute.source`), classifying it (`execute.kind`), asking the user
(`execute.init`).

functions.name: clean
functions.snippet:
local function clean(data)
  local out = {}
  for _, line in ipairs(data or {}) do
    out[#out + 1] = (line:gsub("\r$", ""))
  end
  while #out > 0 and out[#out] == "" do
    out[#out] = nil
  end
  return out
end
functions.summary: The lines of a command's output with line-ending noise removed.

functions.name: to_lines
functions.summary: Split output text into lines.

functions.name: run_ex
functions.snippet:
local function run_ex(commands)
  local lines = {}
  for _, cmd in ipairs(commands) do
    local ok, res = pcall(vim.api.nvim_exec2, cmd, { output = true })
    if not ok then
      lines[#lines + 1] = tostring(res)
      return { ok = false, lines = lines }
    end
    vim.list_extend(lines, to_lines(res.output or ""))
  end
  return { ok = true, lines = lines }
end
functions.summary: Run Ex commands.

functions.name: run_lua
functions.summary: Run a Lua chunk.

functions.name: run_shell
functions.snippet:
local function run_shell(commands, cb)
  local lines = {}
  local function step(i)
    if i > #commands then
      return cb({ ok = true, lines = lines })
    end
    local cmd = commands[i]
    if #commands > 1 then
      lines[#lines + 1] = "$ " .. cmd
    end
    local out, err = {}, {}
    local id = vim.fn.jobstart(cmd, {
      stdout_buffered = true,
      stderr_buffered = true,
      on_stdout = function(_, data)
        out = clean(data)
      end,
      on_stderr = function(_, data)
        err = clean(data)
      end,
      on_exit = function(_, code)
        vim.schedule(function()
          vim.list_extend(lines, out)
          vim.list_extend(lines, err)
          if code ~= 0 then
            lines[#lines + 1] = ("[exit %d]"):format(code)
            return cb({ ok = false, lines = lines })
          end
          step(i + 1)
        end)
      end,
    })
    if id <= 0 then
      lines[#lines + 1] = ("cannot start: %s"):format(cmd)
      cb({ ok = false, lines = lines })
    end
  end
  step(1)
end
functions.summary: Run shell command lines one after the other.

local function fill_current(lines)
  local buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  vim.bo[buf].buftype = "nofile"
  vim.bo[buf].bufhidden = "wipe"
  vim.bo[buf].swapfile = false
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, lines)
  vim.bo[buf].modifiable = false
end

functions.name: copy
functions.snippet:
local function copy(text, what)
  local ok = require("lib.nvim.cross.copy_to_clipboard")(text)
  if ok then
    notify.info("Copied " .. what)
  else
    notify.error("Could not write to the clipboard")
  end
  return ok and true or false
end
functions.summary: Copy text to the + register and say so.

functions.name: M.deliver
functions.snippet:
function M.deliver(how, res, plan)
  local lines = res.lines
  local title = plan.display:match("^[^\n]*") or "Execute"

  if how == "result" then
    copy(table.concat(lines, "\n"), ("%d line(s) of output"):format(#lines))
    return
  end

  if how == "run" then
    if #lines == 0 then
      if plan.kind == "shell" then
        notify.info(res.ok and "done, no output" or "failed, no output")
      end
      return
    end
    (res.ok and notify.info or notify.error)(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
    return
  end

  local shown = #lines > 0 and lines or { "(no output)" }
  if how == "float" then
    require("lib.nvim.output.viewer").show_lines(title, shown)
  elseif how == "split" then
    vim.cmd("new")
    fill_current(shown)
  elseif how == "vsplit" then
    vim.cmd("vnew")
    fill_current(shown)
  elseif how == "tab" then
    vim.cmd("tabnew")
    fill_current(shown)
  end
end
functions.summary: Show or copy what a run gave.

nodes.name: source.lua
nodes.summary: The command needs one answer to "what is the user pointing at?".
nodes.body:
This module gives it, in a fixed order when the user does not say (`from = "auto"`):

  1. a range / Visual selection      (`:'<,'>Execute`)
  2. the `inline code` span under the cursor
  3. the fenced block (``` or ~~~) the cursor is inside
  4. the current line

`from` pins one of them (`selection`, `backtick`, `fence`, `line`, `clipboard`), so a typo in the
text never silently turns into another source.

Key responsibilities:
 - `backtick_at` / `fence_at`: the two text-shape finders, pure (a string or a list of lines in,
   text out), so they are tested without a window
 - `get`: reads the current buffer / the clipboard and applies the order above

Not its job: deciding whether the text is Ex, Lua or shell (`execute.kind`), running it
(`execute.sink`), the command itself (`execute.init`).

functions.name: M.backtick_at

returns.desc: the text between the backticks, trimmed
returns.name: inner

functions.snippet:
function M.backtick_at(line, col)
  local runs = {} ---@type { s: integer, e: integer }[]
  local pos = 1
  while true do
    local s, e = line:find("`+", pos)
    if not s or not e then
      break
    end
    runs[#runs + 1] = { s = s, e = e }
    pos = e + 1
  end
  local i = 1
  while i <= #runs do
    local open = runs[i]
    local width = open.e - open.s + 1
    local partner
    for j = i + 1, #runs do
      if runs[j].e - runs[j].s + 1 == width then
        partner = j
        break
      end
    end
    if not partner then
      i = i + 1
    else
      local close = runs[partner]
      -- `col` is 0-based, the run positions are 1-based
      if col + 1 >= open.s and col + 1 <= close.e then
        local inner = vim.trim(line:sub(open.e + 1, close.s - 1))
        return inner ~= "" and inner or nil
      end
      i = partner + 1
    end
  end
  return nil
end

functions.name: M.fence_at

returns.desc: first word of the info string, lower-cased; nil when there is none
returns.name: lang

functions.snippet:
function M.fence_at(lines, row)
  local open_row, char, width, lang
  for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
    if not open_row then
      local ticks, info = line:match("^%s*(```+)%s*(.-)%s*$")
      if not ticks then
        ticks, info = line:match("^%s*(~~~+)%s*(.-)%s*$")
      end
      -- a backtick fence cannot carry a backtick in its info string (that would be an inline span)
      if ticks and not (ticks:sub(1, 1) == "`" and info:find("`", 1, true)) then
        open_row, char, width = i, ticks:sub(1, 1), #ticks
        local first = info:match("^(%S+)")
        lang = first and first:lower() or nil
      end
    else
      local run = line:match("^%s*(" .. (char == "`" and "`+" or "~+") .. ")%s*$")
      if run and #run >= width then
        if row >= open_row and row <= i then
          return vim.list_slice(lines, open_row + 1, i - 1), lang
        end
        open_row = nil
      end
    end
  end
  if open_row and row >= open_row then
    return vim.list_slice(lines, open_row + 1, #lines), lang
  end
  return nil, nil
end

local function selection_lines(bufnr, range)
  -- has_range() (checked by every caller) guarantees both lines are set
  local l1 = range.line1 --[[@as integer]]
  local l2 = range.line2 --[[@as integer]]
  local m1, m2 = vim.fn.getpos("'<"), vim.fn.getpos("'>")
  local charwise = range.mode == "v" and m1[2] == l1 and m2[2] == l2
  if not charwise then
    return vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, l1 - 1, l2, false)
  end
  local c1, c2 = m1[3], m2[3]
  local last = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, l2 - 1, l2, false)[1] or ""
  -- `'>` points at the first byte of the last selected character: take the whole (multibyte) character
  local stop = c2 - 1
  if c2 >= 1 and c2 <= #last then
    stop = c2 + vim.str_utf_end(last, c2)
  end
  stop = math.min(stop, #last)
  local ok, got = pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text, bufnr, l1 - 1, c1 - 1, l2 - 1, stop, {})
  if ok then
    return got
  end
  return vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, l1 - 1, l2, false)
end

nodes.name: learn_plan_viewer
nodes.summary: `:LearnPlanViewer [week N]` — standalone viewer for the CLI-Lernplan week pages (`docs/ROADMAP/CLI_Lernplan/week-NN.md`).
nodes.body:
Independent of the `learn-cli.nvim` plugin (which stays disabled, see `docs/ROADMAP/LONG_RUN/learn-cli.nvim.md`, "Grundsatzfrage") — this is a thin buffer + two keymaps + a checkbox toggle, not a second exercise engine.

Opens a week page in a normal buffer for navigation/editing (checkbox
toggling), and can additionally push the current week to the browser via
mdview.nvim (`:MDView start`) for reading.

Commands:
  :LearnPlanViewer            resume at the last-opened week (or week 1)
  :LearnPlanViewer week N     jump straight to week N

Buffer-local keymaps (only in a week-page buffer):
  <leader>ln   next week
  <leader>lp   previous week
  <leader>lx   toggle the checkbox on the current line
  <leader>lb   open the current week in the browser (mdview.nvim)

  end

end

  if count == 0 then

functions.name: open_week
functions.snippet:
local function open_week(n)
  if not valid_week(n) then
    notify.error(("Woche %s existiert nicht (1-%d)"):format(tostring(n), config.week_count))
    return
  end

  local path = config.week_path(n)
  if vim.fn.filereadable(path) ~= 1 then
    notify.error("Seite fehlt: " .. path)
    return
  end

  -- Reuse an already-open week buffer's window instead of stacking splits.
  for bufnr, week in pairs(open_weeks) do
    if week == n and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(bufnr) then
      local win = vim.fn.bufwinid(bufnr)
      if win ~= -1 then
        vim.api.nvim_set_current_win(win)
        remember_week(n)
        return
      end
    end
  end

  vim.cmd("edit " .. vim.fn.fnameescape(path))
  local bufnr = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
  open_weeks[bufnr] = n
  remember_week(n)

  ---@param ... any
  local function map(...)
    vim.keymap.set(...)
  end
  local opts = { buffer = bufnr, silent = true }
  map("n", "<leader>ln", function()
    open_week(n + 1)
  end, vim.tbl_extend("force", opts, { desc = "Lernplan: nächste Woche" }))
  map("n", "<leader>lp", function()
    open_week(n - 1)
  end, vim.tbl_extend("force", opts, { desc = "Lernplan: vorige Woche" }))

nodes.name: native_repos
nodes.summary: Sister of `:MyPlugins` for the native apps (tasks-desktop, rules-desktop, ai-desktop, takt, docmap-desktop, appkit; the list is…
nodes.body:
They are no lazy specs, so `:MyPlugins` never sees them.

 - `list`           per app: cloned or not, git state, and whether the build is current (artifact older than the
                    newest commit of its sources = stale, same rule as `scripts/sync-machine.ps1`)
 - `clone [name]`   clone what is missing (additive, never overwrites)
 - `pull [name]`    fast-forward the clean ones (`--ff-only`; dirty or ahead is left alone and said so)
 - `deps [name]`    check the tools the apps build with (`toolchain.lua`) and install the missing ones that need
                    no administrator (rustup, tauri-cli, the MSYS2 packages); the others are named
 - `build [name]`   run the build command of an app (its scripts/build-install.ps1 -BuildOnly); without a name,
                    every STALE or missing build one after the other. Apps without a command only show their
                    hint, apps with a missing tool are skipped. Output goes to the quickfix list. Never installs
                    or starts anything.
 - `install [name]` `deps`, then build and install for the current user from the terminal, no downloaded
                    setup.exe (which SmartScreen stops on a managed workstation); without a name, every cloned
                    app. Output goes to the quickfix list.
 - `uninstall [name]` scripts/uninstall.ps1 of the app; without a name, every cloned app.

On the workstation (`require("machine").is("workstation")`, from NVIM_MACHINE_ROLE) `build`, `install`
and `deps` refuse with a message: an own unsigned program is what the EDR (Falcon) reports there.
`list`, `clone`, `pull` and `uninstall` stay allowed (`lua/machine_guard.lua`).

params.desc: Seconds of the newest commit touching the sources, nil when unknown

functions.snippet:
function M.build_state(artifact_mtime, source_commit_time)
  if not artifact_mtime then
    return "missing"
  end
  if source_commit_time and source_commit_time > artifact_mtime then
    return "stale"
  end
  return "current"
end
functions.summary: Staleness rule: the artifact is stale when a source commit is newer than it.

functions.name: state_of
functions.snippet:
local function state_of(native, dir)
  if not uv.fs_stat(dir) then
    return "not cloned"
  end
  if not native.artifact then
    return "no artifact"
  end
  local stat = uv.fs_stat(dir .. "/" .. native.artifact)
  local cmd = { "git", "-C", dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%ct", "--" }
  vim.list_extend(cmd, native.sources or { "." })
  local res = vim.system(cmd, { text = true }):wait()
  local commit_time = res.code == 0 and tonumber(vim.trim(res.stdout or "")) or nil
  return M.build_state(stat and stat.mtime.sec or nil, commit_time)
end

functions.name: git_state
functions.snippet:
local function git_state(dir)
  local res = vim
    .system({ "git", "-C", dir, "status", "--porcelain", "--branch" }, { text = true })
    :wait()
  if res.code ~= 0 then
    return "no git"
  end
  local lines = vim.split(res.stdout or "", "\r?\n", { trimempty = true })
  local parts = {}
  local branch = lines[1] or ""
  local behind = branch:match("behind (%d+)")
  local ahead = branch:match("ahead (%d+)")
  if behind then
    parts[#parts + 1] = "behind " .. behind
  end
  if ahead then
    parts[#parts + 1] = "ahead " .. ahead
  end
  if #lines > 1 then
    parts[#parts + 1] = "dirty"
  end
  return #parts > 0 and table.concat(parts, ", ") or "clean"
end

    return natives.list

functions.name: M.list
functions.snippet:
function M.list()
  local base = base_dir()
  if not base then
    return
  end
  local out, attention = {}, false
  for _, native in ipairs(natives.list) do
    local dir = base .. "/" .. native.name
    local build = state_of(native, dir)
    local git = build == "not cloned" and "-" or git_state(dir)
    out[#out + 1] = ("%-15s git: %-14s build: %s"):format(native.name, git, build)
    attention = attention or build == "not cloned" or build == "stale" or build == "missing"
  end
  local text = table.concat(out, "\n")
  if attention then
    notify.warn(text)
  else
    notify.info(text)
  end
end

functions.name: M.clone
functions.snippet:
function M.clone(only)
  local base = base_dir()
  if not base then
    return
  end
  local todo = selected(only)
  ops.run_sequential(todo, function(native, on_done)
    ops.clone_one({ repo = native.repo, name = native.name }, base, function(status, err)
      on_done(status ~= "failed", err)
    end)
  end, function(native)
    return native.name
  end, function(ok_items, failed)
    local lines = { ("%d native repo(s) handled"):format(#ok_items) }
    for _, f in ipairs(failed) do
      lines[#lines + 1] = ("%s failed: %s"):format(f.item.name, f.err)
    end
    if #failed > 0 then
      notify.warn(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
    else
      notify.info(table.concat(lines, "\n"))
    end
  end)
end

functions.name: M.pull
functions.snippet:
function M.pull(only)
  local base = base_dir()
  if not base then
    return
  end
  local notes = {}
  ops.run_sequential(selected(only), function(native, on_done)
    local dir = base .. "/" .. native.name
    if not uv.fs_stat(dir) then
      notes[#notes + 1] = native.name .. ": not cloned"
      on_done(true)
      return
    end
    ops.check_removable(dir, function(safe, reason)
      if not safe then
        notes[#notes + 1] = ("%s: left alone (%s)"):format(native.name, reason or "dirty or ahead")
        on_done(true)
        return
      end
      ops.pull_one(dir, function(ok, err, changed)
        if ok then
          notes[#notes + 1] = native.name .. (changed and ": pulled" or ": up to date")
        end
        on_done(ok, err)
      end)
    end)
  end, function(native)
    return native.name
  end, function(_, failed)
    for _, f in ipairs(failed) do
      notes[#notes + 1] = ("%s: pull failed: %s"):format(f.item.name, f.err)
    end
    local text = table.concat(notes, "\n")
    if #failed > 0 then
      notify.warn(text)
    else
      notify.info(text)
    end
  end)
end

functions.name: run
functions.snippet:
local function run(kind, only)
  -- build and install make a native program run on this machine; on the workstation that is
  -- what the EDR reports, so only the uninstall goes on there
  if kind ~= "uninstall" and workstation.refused(":MyNative " .. kind) then
    return
  end
  local base = base_dir()
  if not base then
    return
  end
  if running then
    notify.warn("A build or install is already running")
    return
  end
  local candidates, states = selected(only), {}
  for _, native in ipairs(candidates) do
    local dir = base .. "/" .. native.name
    -- only a build asks git for the staleness; install and uninstall need nothing but "cloned"
    if kind == "build" then
      states[native.name] = state_of(native, dir)
    else
      states[native.name] = uv.fs_stat(dir) and "cloned" or "not cloned"
    end
  end
  local todo, hints
  if kind == "build" then
    todo, hints = M.plan_build(candidates, states, only ~= nil)
  else
    todo, hints =
      M.plan_install(candidates, states, only ~= nil, kind --[[@as "install"|"uninstall"]])
  end
  if #todo == 0 then
    if #hints > 0 then
      notify.info("Nothing to " .. kind .. " from here:\n" .. table.concat(hints, "\n"))
    elseif kind == "build" then
      notify.info("All builds are current.")
    else
      notify.info(("Nothing to %s (no cloned app has that command)."):format(kind))
    end
    return

function M.deps(only)

  if running then

  end, selected(only))

function M.split(natives, missing)
  local ready, held = {}, {}
  for _, native in ipairs(natives) do

function M.check(ids, tools)
  local known = by_id(tools)
  local missing = {}
  for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
    local tool = known[id]

nodes.name: plugin_repos
nodes.summary: source mode of the personal plugin list — plus an interactive picker, a dashboard and the wkdbook task commands.
nodes.body:
Registers a single `:MyPlugins {clone|remove|fetch|pull|update|sync|reclone| dashboard|mode|list|jumpTo|picker|tasks|task|open} [args]` command via `lib.nvim.bindings.usercmd.composer` (replaces the former flat `:MyPluginsClone` / `:MyPluginsRemove`). The `tasks`, `task` and `open` routes come from `tasks_nvim.ui.routes` (the plugin `tasks.nvim`: handlers, engine) and are not limited to the plugin list: they work on the areas of the wkdbook vault. `sync` (routes in `sync_routes.lua`, orchestrator `sync.lua`) is the thorough `update`: fetch every listed repo, pull what is behind, triage the rest.

Every subcommand except `dashboard` (which just opens gitsuite.nvim's
own `:Git dashboard`) operates only on the repos `plugins.personal.core.list`
names against `dir`/`$REPOS_DIR` — never on whatever a directory scan
turns up, unlike `:Git dashboard update`, because `$REPOS_DIR` also holds
non-plugin checkouts (Notes, WKDBooks, ...) a scan-and-delete would put
at risk. `remove`/`reclone` only touch repos confirmed clean via `git
status --porcelain --branch`, named in a single confirmation prompt
first; `fetch`/`pull`/`update` are the two-machine `dir`-mode sync tool.

Full per-command docs, the safety-model rationale and the two-machine
workflow: see `README.md` in this directory.

local function clone_all(path, only_name, dry_run)
  local base_dir = resolve_base_dir(path)
  if not base_dir then
    notify.error("No repository directory provided and REPOS_DIR is not set")
    return
  end

  local stat = loop.fs_stat(base_dir)
  if not stat or stat.type ~= "directory" then
    notify.error("Repository directory is not accessible: " .. base_dir)
    return
  end

  local entries, err = plugin_list.read_for_clone()
  if not entries then
    notify.error(tostring(err))
    return
  end

  if only_name then
    local filtered = {}
    for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
      if entry.name == only_name then
        filtered[#filtered + 1] = entry
      end
    end
    entries = filtered
  end

  -- `ops.clone_one`'s own "exists" branch is exactly `loop.fs_stat(target)`
  -- with no git call in between — so dry-run can reuse that same predicate
  -- synchronously here instead of running clone_one and discarding the
  -- would-be clone, which is the only bit of work a preview needs.
  if dry_run then
    local would_clone, existing = {}, {}
    for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
      if loop.fs_stat(base_dir .. "/" .. entry.name) then
        existing[#existing + 1] = entry.name
      else
        would_clone[#would_clone + 1] = entry.name

finish_check = function(safe, unsafe, base_dir)
  if #unsafe > 0 then
    notify.warn("Left alone (not clean, not deleted):\n" .. table.concat(unsafe, "\n"))
  end

  if #safe == 0 then
    notify.info("Nothing left to remove — every present plugin has uncommitted or unpushed work.")
    return
  end

  local msg = ("Permanently delete %d repositor%s from %s?\n\n%s"):format(
    #safe,
    #safe == 1 and "y" or "ies",
    base_dir,
    table.concat(safe, "\n")
  )
  confirm.yesno(msg, "delete", function(accepted)
    if not accepted then
      notify.info("Cancelled — nothing deleted.")
      return
    end

    local removed, remove_failed = {}, {}
    for _, name in ipairs(safe) do
      local target = base_dir .. "/" .. name
      local ok = fn.delete(target, "rf")
      if ok == 0 then
        removed[#removed + 1] = name
      else
        remove_failed[#remove_failed + 1] = name

    end

    if #remove_failed > 0 then
      notify.error(
        ("Removed %d, failed to remove: %s"):format(#removed, table.concat(remove_failed, ", "))
      )
    else
      notify.info(("Removed %d repositor%s"):format(#removed, #removed == 1 and "y" or "ies"))
    end

local function run_listed_op(gerund, past, op_fn, path, only_name, on_complete)
  local function finish()
    if on_complete then
      on_complete()
    end
  end

  local present, base_dir = present_listed_names(path, only_name)
  if not present then
    finish()
    return
  end
  if #present == 0 then
    notify.info("None of the listed plugins are present in " .. tostring(base_dir))
    finish()
    return
  end

  local prog = new_progress(("[usrcmds.plugin_repos] %s"):format(gerund:lower()))
  notify.info(("%s %d plugin(s) in %s..."):format(gerund, #present, base_dir))

  local changed_count, unchanged_count = 0, 0

  ops.run_sequential(present, function(name, on_done)
    op_fn(base_dir .. "/" .. name, function(ok, err, changed)
      if ok and changed ~= nil then
        if changed then
          changed_count = changed_count + 1
        else
          unchanged_count = unchanged_count + 1
        end
      end
      on_done(ok, err)
    end)
  end, function(name)
    return name
  end, function(ok_items, failed)
    if prog then
      prog:finish(("%d %s, %d failed"):format(#ok_items, past, #failed))
    end

functions.snippet:
local function resolve_current_plugin_name(base_dir)
  -- `fnamemodify(..., ":p")` on Windows keeps backslashes, so normalize them
  -- to "/" here too -- otherwise this always fails to match, since the
  -- candidate side below already converts every "\" to "/".
  local normalized_base = (fnamemodify(base_dir, ":p"):gsub("\\", "/"):gsub("/+$", "")) .. "/"
  local candidates = { vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0), fn.getcwd() }

  local entries = plugin_list.read() or {}
  for _, candidate in ipairs(candidates) do
    if candidate and candidate ~= "" then
      local normalized = fnamemodify(candidate, ":p"):gsub("\\", "/")
      -- Windows paths (and drive letters in particular) are case-insensitive
      -- -- $REPOS_DIR's casing need not match what getcwd()/the buffer name
      -- happens to report.
      local base_prefix = normalized:sub(1, #normalized_base)
      local prefix_matches = is_windows and base_prefix:lower() == normalized_base:lower()
        or base_prefix == normalized_base
      if prefix_matches then
        local name = normalized:sub(#normalized_base + 1):match("^([^/]+)")
        if name then
          for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
            if entry.name == name then
              return name
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function open_dashboard(path, fetch_mode)
  local function open()
    vim.cmd("Git dashboard" .. (path and (" " .. fn.fnameescape(path)) or ""))
  end

  if not fetch_mode then
    open()
    return
  end

  local base_dir = resolve_base_dir(path)
  if not base_dir then
    notify.error("No repository directory provided and REPOS_DIR is not set")
    return
  end

  if fetch_mode == "this" then
    local name = resolve_current_plugin_name(base_dir)
    if not name then
      notify.warn(
        "Could not resolve the current buffer/cwd to a listed plugin — opening the dashboard without fetching."
      )
      open()
      return
    end
    fetch_all(path, name, open)
    return
  end

  fetch_all(path, nil, open)
end

functions.snippet:
local function unlisted_all(path)
  local base_dir = resolve_base_dir(path)
  if not base_dir then
    notify.error("no repos directory resolved; set $REPOS_DIR or pass one")
    return
  end

  local ok, specs = pcall(require, "plugins.personal")
  if not ok or type(specs) ~= "table" then
    notify.error("cannot load plugins.personal: " .. tostring(specs))
    return
  end
  local known = {}
  for _, spec in ipairs(specs) do
    if type(spec[1]) == "string" then
      known[fn.fnamemodify(spec[1], ":t")] = true
    end
  end

  local lines = {}
  for name, kind in vim.fs.dir(base_dir) do
    local dir = base_dir .. "/" .. name
    local is_folder = kind == "directory" or (kind == "link" and fn.isdirectory(dir) == 1)
    if is_folder and name:match("%.nvim$") and not known[name] then
      -- A plugin checkout has Lua to load; a bare `.nvim` folder (notes,
      -- archive) is not a candidate.
      local has_code = fn.isdirectory(dir .. "/lua") == 1 or fn.isdirectory(dir .. "/plugin") == 1
      -- Own repos only: a third-party clone (plenary.nvim) is never "to be
      -- added". `.git` as a file (worktree) has no config to read; keep it.
      local git_config = dir .. "/.git/config"
      local own = true
      if fn.filereadable(git_config) == 1 then
        own = table.concat(fn.readfile(git_config), "\n"):find("StefanBartl", 1, true) ~= nil
      end
      if has_code and own then
        local has_bindings = fn.filereadable(dir .. "/docs/BINDINGS.md") == 1
        lines[#lines + 1] = ("%-24s  %s"):format(
          name,
          has_bindings and "BINDINGS.md" or "no BINDINGS.md"
        )

local function write_override(new_mode)
  local path = source_file_path()
  local ok, lines = pcall(fn.readfile, path)
  if not ok then
    return false, "cannot read " .. path
  end
  for i, line in ipairs(lines) do
    local prefix, suffix = line:match('^(local%s+OVERRIDE%s*=%s*)"[%a]+"(.*)$')
    if prefix then
      lines[i] = prefix .. '"' .. new_mode .. '"' .. suffix
      fn.writefile(lines, path)
      return true, nil
    end
  end
  return false, "OVERRIDE line not found in " .. path
end

function M.enable()
  -- Directory arg: real directory completion plus `$REPOS_DIR` offered up
  -- front when resolvable, mirroring gitsuite.nvim's directory-argument
  -- completion. Validation is otherwise the built-in DIR
  -- semantics (must expand to an existing directory).
  composer.register_type("MYPLUGINS_DIR", {
    -- `desc`: the line lib.nvim's option float shows for the positional argument of every route that
    -- takes one (all mean the same: the folder the checkouts live in).
    desc = "Folder with the plugin checkouts (default: $REPOS_DIR)",
    validate = function(raw)
      local expanded = expand_path(raw)
      if not is_dir(fnamemodify(expanded, ":p")) then
        return false, nil, ("'%s' is not a directory"):format(raw)
      end
      return true, expanded, nil
    end,
    complete = function(arg_lead)
      local candidates = {}
      if env.REPOS_DIR and env.REPOS_DIR ~= "" and ("$REPOS_DIR"):sub(1, #arg_lead) == arg_lead then
        candidates[#candidates + 1] = "$REPOS_DIR"
      end
      vim.list_extend(candidates, fn.getcompletion(arg_lead, "dir"))
      return candidates
    end,
  })

  -- `--only=<name>` for clone/remove: validated and completed against the
  -- *live* plugins.personal.core.list on every request (not a snapshot taken once
  -- at registration time), same principle reposcope.nvim's own per-request
  -- completers use — the list only changes on a config edit anyway, but
  -- there is no reason to risk a stale copy for a lookup this cheap.
  composer.register_type("MYPLUGINS_NAME", {
    validate = function(raw)
      local entries = plugin_list.read_for_clone()
      for _, entry in ipairs(entries or {}) do
        if entry.name == raw then
          return true, raw, nil
        end
      end
      return false, nil, ("'%s' is not in plugins.personal.core.list"):format(raw)
